editorial.summary: A Big Bear recording retreat built around Money Mark and Steve Lee's album begins with severe eating-disorder behavior. David describes diabetes risk, chewing and spitting cheesecake, pizza and donuts, intermittent vomiting, procedural pro-mia/pro-ana advice, weakened gag response and blood. The transcript preserves every claim while the editorial layer rejects the ranking of anorexia or bulimia as effective, excludes purging instructions from previews, and distinguishes a recurring health-podcast joke from clinical authority. After the explicit six-person introduction, the episode turns to a growing Bible study at David's parents' home. Bill Poon's concealed Christianity, Steve's conversion and psychedelic departure, speaking in tongues, Andy Milonakis, karma, atheism, agnosticism, cult jokes and each participant's religious history build into David's account of forced baptisms, prison faith, bargaining with God, release from Japanese jail, giving away possessions and service as human purpose. The same discussion preserves Steve's reptilian, Pleiadian, Nibiru, lower-astral and child-fear claims as beliefs rather than fact. The crossroads moves from a devil bargain in Ralph Macchio's film to a practical decision metaphor. The second half ties service to labor: rather than hire Steve, David offers paid leave from Fat Sal's to record, discusses family and Brazil/Macau travel, then recounts a compulsive rebound after being catfished. He reports eight sexual sessions, persuading a doctor to prescribe tadalafil, shaving an unmeasured dose, palpitations, flushing, headache, rough sex after a partner begged him to stop, bleeding/injury claims, and a painful bump ultimately diagnosed as an ingrown hair. Medication, arousal and prior participation never override a stop. The title comes from the cast's simplified explanation that ED drugs still require being 'horny in your heart.' Private partners, athletes, medical records and images remain protected. The closing sections cover a hostess club, a webcam-performer date, an applicant, late-night fans and an escalating persistent-fan encounter that Critter resolves without violence. Music and film trivia supplies multiple proper-noun corrections. Twenty-seven empty records and one 22.16-second `mik` decoder loop are removed; the surrounding indistinct-audio marker and intelligible birthday/sign-off speech remain. Every idea and slur stays attributable, but dangerous instructions, private-person dossiers and named dialogue do not ship.
